nodes.summary: For every subgroup $G$ of the group of permutations of $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$ that is isomorphic to the additive group $(\mathbb{Q}, +)$, there is an element $g \in G$ such that the set of displacements $\{a - g(a) : a \in \mathbb{N}\}$, computed in $\mathbb{Z}$, is infinite. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 20.98 is yes.
nodes.title: Permutation groups isomorphic to the rationals have infinite displacement (Kourovka 20.98)
